title: Can LLMs Speak For Diverse People? Tuning LLMs via Debate to Generate Controllable Controversial Statements
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the controllability of LLMs in generating statements that adhere to a user-defined stance on controversial topics, including stances based on religious objections (e.g., religious objections to mandatory organ donation), without defaulting to a biased or neutral response.
findings: Existing LLMs like Vicuna 7B v1.5 fail to adhere to user-defined stances based on religious objections. When prompted to argue against mandatory organ donation from a religious perspective, the model ignored the user's stance and instead argued in favor of organ donation, which could be perceived as offensive. The proposed DEBATUNE method significantly improved model controllability, enabling the LLM to generate high-quality statements that strictly supported the user's requested religious viewpoint.
